description:
A long conversation re-lexes every prior assistant message every frame. Cache rendered output per finalized message so that finalized history is effectively free to redraw.

Builds on `.3` — the cache lives inside the render-state container introduced there.

## Why

`render_transcript` walks every entry on every render. Each `AssistantMessage.render()` calls `Markdown.new()` fresh, which re-runs `EarmarkParser.as_ast` + `SyntaxHighlight` + `WrapAnsi` over the full message text. Conversation history is immutable once `MessageEnd` has fired, so this work is purely wasted.

Confirm via `.2`'s analysis #4 that `transcript.render` cost grows with `msg_count` (and not only with the streaming message's `text_bytes`) before starting; if it doesn't, this ticket is moot.

## Code references

- `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/interactive.ex:1754` — `render_transcript`; iterates messages.
- `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/interactive.ex:2197-2198` — per-assistant render call site.
- `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/components/assistant_message.ex` — `AssistantMessage` struct/render; this is where cache reads/writes wire in.
- `apps/octo_pi_tui/lib/octo_pi/tui/components/markdown.ex:40-50` — current `Markdown.render`; the cached output is its return value.
- `OctoPi.Agent.Event.MessageEnd` (alias used in `interactive.ex:23`) — finalize event; this is when a streaming message becomes eligible for caching.

## Shape

Cache structure on `Interactive`'s render state (or in `.3`'s render-state container):

```
%{
  rendered_lines: %{message_id => %{
    content_hash: binary,   # hash of message text
    width:        integer,
    lines:        [iolist],
    line_count:   integer
  }}
}
```

Read path on render:

1. For each finalized assistant message, look up by `message_id`.
2. If `content_hash` and `width` both match, reuse `lines`.
3. Otherwise, render fresh, store, and return.

Write path:

- On `MessageEnd`, render the message once and populate the cache. The streaming message is intentionally **not** cached during streaming — `.5` handles its incremental render.
- On width change (terminal resize), invalidate all entries (clear the map). Re-render lazily on next access.
- On theme/syntax-highlight setting change, invalidate by clearing the map. Don't try to be cleverer than that.

`message_id` source: every assistant message struct carries an `id` field via `OctoPi.Agent.Event.MessageEnd.message`/`.MessageStart.message`. Confirm and thread that ID through the render call sites if it isn't already.

## Acceptance

- `transcript.render.duration` becomes flat in `msg_count` for finalized messages — verify against `.2`'s baseline.
- A first render of a finalized message populates the cache; subsequent renders show no `markdown.render` span emitted for that message (cache hit short-circuits).
- Width change clears entries; the next render rebuilds all of them.
- Memory growth is bounded by transcript size and dominated by `lines` content; no observable allocation churn for unchanged messages between frames.

## Tests

- Add to `apps/octo_pi_tui/test/octo_pi/tui/interactive_test.exs`: cache hit/miss invariants under `MessageEnd`, resize-invalidates-all, theme-change-invalidates-all.
- Verify via telemetry handlers (no `markdown.render` span fires for cached messages) — keeps the test independent of internal representation.
title: Cache rendered lines per finalized message
